Part 2&3 人物 PEOPLE AI 补全经历

Describe a person who likes to look after the natural world

描述一个喜欢保护自然的人

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a person who likes to look after the natural world

  • Who this person is (这个人是谁)
  • What he or she does (他/她做什么)
  • How he or she does it (他/她怎么做)
  • How often he or she does it (他/她多久做一次)
  • And explain how you feel about this person (并谈谈你对这个人的感受)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a person who likes to look after the natural world

I'd like to talk about my girlfriend, who is the most nature-loving person I know. She genuinely cares about the environment, and being around her has changed the way I see nature. First of all, who she is: she's my girlfriend, and we've been together for a while now. What she does to protect nature is quite simple but meaningful. She loves the sea, so we often go to Qianhai and Shenzhen Bay, which are both by the water. Every time we go, she brings a bag with her, and she picks up any litter she sees on the beach, like plastic bottles and food wrappers. The way she does it is what impresses me. She doesn't make a big show of it, she just quietly collects rubbish while we walk, and she always takes her own drink bottles home instead of leaving them behind. When we went hiking in Yangjiang, she did the same thing on the mountain, reminding me not to drop anything either. As for how often, it's basically every time we're outdoors, so at least a couple of times a month. The reason I admire her is that she doesn't just say she loves nature, she actually acts on it. I used to think nature was just something nice to look at, but she's taught me that caring for it means taking responsibility. Looking back, I think people like her make the world a better place, one small action at a time.

讲的是女朋友，我认识的最爱自然的人。她爱海，我们常去前海和深圳湾，每次去她都带个袋子，把沙滩上的塑料瓶、食品包装等垃圾捡走。她做这些很低调，不张扬，边走边默默捡，自己的饮料瓶也带回家；去阳江爬山时她在山上也这么做，还提醒我不要乱扔。频率是每次户外活动都这样，一个月至少几次。佩服她是因为她不只是嘴上说爱自然，而是真的行动；她让我明白爱护自然意味着承担责任。

Q2Do you think parents should teach their children how to protect the environment?

Definitely, I think parents play a crucial role here. Children learn most of their habits at home, so if parents teach them to sort rubbish, save water and not litter, these behaviours become natural. It's much easier to form good habits in childhood than to change bad ones later. Parents can also lead by example, since children tend to copy what they see. So I'd say environmental education should definitely start at home.

父母绝对扮演关键角色。孩子大部分习惯是在家养成的，如果父母教他们垃圾分类、节约用水、不乱扔垃圾，这些行为就会变成自然习惯。童年养成好习惯比以后改掉坏习惯容易得多。父母还可以以身作则，孩子会模仿看到的行为。环保教育应该从家里开始。

Q3What laws about the environment are effective in your country?

In my country, a few environmental laws have been quite effective. The most visible one is the waste sorting policy in major cities, which requires people to separate their rubbish into different categories, and it has noticeably changed daily habits. There are also restrictions on single-use plastics, like plastic bags, which are no longer free in supermarkets. On top of that, strict emission standards for factories have helped improve air quality in many areas. So I'd say these practical regulations have made a real difference.

国内有几项环保法律效果不错。最明显的是大城市的垃圾分类政策，要求居民把垃圾分门别类，明显改变了日常习惯；还有一次性塑料限制，超市塑料袋不再免费；另外工厂严格的排放标准改善了很多地区的空气质量。这些务实的法规确实带来了实际改变。

Q4Which do you think people prefer, rewards or punishment, when it comes to government intervention in environmental protection?

I think most people prefer rewards, because they feel positive and encouraging. For example, subsidies for buying electric cars or discounts for recycling make people want to participate. Punishment, like fines for littering, works too, but it can feel unfair and create resentment. That said, some punishment is necessary for serious violations, since not everyone responds to encouragement. So on balance, I'd say a combination works best, with rewards as the main tool and punishment as a backup.

多数人更喜欢奖励，因为奖励让人感觉积极、受鼓励；比如买电动车的补贴、回收的折扣会让人愿意参与。惩罚（如乱扔垃圾罚款）也有效，但可能让人觉得不公平、产生抵触。不过对严重违规，一定惩罚是必要的，因为不是所有人都吃鼓励这套。总体奖励为主、惩罚为辅的组合最好。

Q5Is it easy for children in cities to get close to the natural world?

I'd say it's harder for city children than for those in the countryside. In cities, nature is often limited to parks and gardens, and many children spend most of their time indoors with screens. That said, it's not impossible, since most cities have parks, and some families take children to the seaside or mountains on weekends. So while city children have fewer chances to connect with nature, it's still possible if parents make an effort.

城市孩子比农村孩子更难亲近自然。城市里自然往往只有公园和花园，很多孩子大部分时间待在室内对着屏幕。但也不是不可能：大多数城市有公园，有些家庭周末带孩子去海边或山里。城市孩子接触自然的机会少，但只要父母用心还是可以的。

Q6What can people do to protect the natural world?

There are many things ordinary people can do. The most basic ones are reducing waste, like using fewer plastic bags and recycling properly, and saving energy, such as turning off lights and using public transport. People can also make greener choices when shopping, like buying products with less packaging. On a larger scale, supporting environmental organisations or joining clean-up activities makes a difference too. I think small daily actions, done consistently, add up to real change.

普通人能做的事很多。最基本的：减少浪费（少用塑料袋、正确回收）、节约能源（关灯、坐公共交通）；购物时做更环保的选择，比如买包装少的产品；更大层面，支持环保组织或参加清理活动也有作用。小的日常行动坚持做，累积起来就是真正的改变。

Q7Is it important to teach students environmental protection at school?

Yes, I think it's very important. Schools are where children spend most of their time, so environmental education there can reach almost everyone. Teaching students about issues like climate change and waste helps them understand why protecting nature matters, and practical activities, like recycling programmes or tree planting, turn that understanding into habits. Since environmental problems are getting more serious, I believe this kind of education should be a regular part of the curriculum.

非常重要。学校是孩子待得最久的地方，环保教育在那里能覆盖几乎所有人。教学生了解气候变化、垃圾等问题，让他们明白保护自然为什么重要；回收项目、植树这类实践活动把理解变成习惯。环境问题越来越严重，这类教育应该成为课程的常规部分。
